claims: The Cuban Revolutionary Armed Forces (FAR) are centered on a "war of the people" defensive doctrine.
The Cuban Revolutionary Armed Forces (FAR) have an estimated 45,000–50,000 active personnel.
Cuba relies on a paramilitary network with over 1 million personnel.
The military controls roughly 4% of the economy.
The Cuban military is comprised of the Army, Air Force, and Navy.
The Cuban military has a special forces unit known as "Avispas Negras" (Black Wasps).
Cuba has 2-year mandatory service for citizens aged 17–28.
The Cuban military relies on older Soviet-era systems including aging MiG-21, MiG-23, and limited MiG-29 fighters, alongside T-54/55 and T-62 tanks.
The Cuban military recently engaged in joint training with Belarus for air defense systems.
Paramilitary bodies include the Territorial Troops Militia (MTT).
Paramilitary bodies include the Youth Labor Army (EJT).
Border Troops are subordinate to the Interior Ministry.
The military plays a role in the economy through enterprises notably in tourism and construction.
As of March 2026, the military is conducting exercises to prepare for potential external aggression.
Miguel Díaz-Canel is Commander in Chief.
Corps Gen. Álvaro López Miera is Minister of the FAR.
